title: Peak District Prose
shortDescription: A website that allows users to add their stories and for staff to manage users and stories.
longDescription:
A web based story publishing platform was developed using Ruby on Rails, integrating a role-based access control, content management and a virtual credit economy. The system supports Readers, Writers, Premium Readers and Staff with distinct permissions and workflows for each role. 
 Writers can publish priced stories and create configurable polls to gather feedback from subscribers. Readers can purchase stories using Popcorn credits, subscribe to writers and retain access to previously purchased content. Premium memberships introduces discounted Popcorn purchases and additional credit rewards. The platform implements an 80% Popcorn reward for writers on subscriptions, establishing an internal incentive mechanism for content creatoin. 
 A dedicated Staff interface provides account administration, credential resets, account bans and deletion, Popcorn balance adjustments and support-query management. Validation checks enforce business rules, including account eligibility and sufficient credit balance, while reestricting protected functionality to authorised users. 
 The application uses Ruby on Rails controllers to organise request handling and application logic, with database persistence for accounts, stories and related platform data. GitLab supports source-code management and collaborative development. During implementation, redundant controller files were removed and controller responsibilities reorganised by function and user role, improving code clarity and maintainability.
 Technical validation included unit and integration testing, with the report recording 100% passing results for the documented account registration and popcorn management tests. Development followed an iterative, user story driven process using acceptance criteria and burndown charts to track implementation progress.
 The project delivered an integrated publishing and monetisation workflow combining role specific interfaces, persistent content, credit based transactions, subscriptions, feedback collection and administrative oversight. Its principle technical achievement was bringing these interacting features into a single application while maintaining differentiated access rules and a more structured maintainable codebase.
